reviews.title: Fantastic Pregnancy App
reviews.contents:
I’m 22 years young and I’m expecting my first bub. All super exciting however at first it was quite scary because so many places tell you different things about you and the baby each week and some things don’t even make sense. 
I read the reviews for this app and decided I’ll give it go and from previous experience with apps I was thinking this will be just like the rest but I was totally wrong!! No ads popping in and out, the app as far as I’ve had it hasn’t froze. I’ve had the app since I was 2 weeks and I’m now 18 weeks. Due 26th March 2020!! It gives you clear and understanding information you need to know. It’s extremely helpful when you need advice or tips. 
The baby looks so realistic that it does pump you with excitement. 
So I definitely and honestly recommend this app for friends, family and anybody else who is expecting. 
And also I love the fact the app says FREE and not like most apps, you download then they are crafty to snap a payment from you wheres this app doesn’t! So thank you to the person who created this wonderful app.  🤰 100% recommend.🤰

reviews.title: Great functionality but content needs updating
reviews.contents: The app functionality works great - it has never crashed on me or closed expectantly. I’ve enjoyed using this app and check it most days. The content overall is very good - some helpful week by week articles, visualisations of baby week by week etc. If looking for enhancement opportunities I would say refreshing the content would be a great thing to consider as during COVID some of the advice is out of date. Advice like going swimming  - I really wish I could :) - isn’t practical at the moment for 99% of people. Other, newly prescient, advice - like setting up a virtual support network - is missing. I was also disappointed to see that some recent NHS messaging (re not being put off getting help if needed etc) is labelled as “sponsored”. This implies the NHS has to pay for the service which feels discordant with public sentiment and not the right thing to do. If they have paid, I’m disappointed in the company for making that decision. If not and the NHS received it free or at a discount, perhaps add a note to the NHS message as this would be very “feel good” for app users. Secondly, the app could be more inclusive on language for people who are expecting but who don’t identify as female. If I were a man or non binary person I’m not sure I would feel very well catered for in terms of language. This is a super easy fix - just add more options on sign up and be careful how you edit the articles.

reviews.title: Really useful pregnancy app
reviews.contents:
I’ve been using the free version of this app throughout my pregnancy so far and have found it really useful. There are loads of different features available, seeing scans and information about baby’s progress each week has been great and most of the articles are interesting/informative. It’s not a one stop shop and yes you should get antenatal info elsewhere but it’s great to go alongside that. 

I recently purchased the paid for version so I could use the kick counter, however have found this a bit disappointing. It goes off the old way of measuring foetal movements which is whether they kick ten times in a two hour period and it encourages you to do things to make baby move if they don’t. It’s actually now advised to get to know your own baby’s pattern of movement as they are all different and if this is reduced to call a midwife as soon as possible. 

I’m still using the counter throughout the day to track baby’s movement but it’s not really designed to be used in this way as well as it could be and could be better with maybe some charts or something to display their activity?,” I haven’t found any other apps out there that seem to do this well so I’ll stick with this. Hopefully the contraction counter will be handy when the time comes too!

reviews.title: Recommend to every first time mum.
reviews.contents:
Love this app! Used it through my first pregnancy and the everyday articles kept me busy. So many things I didn’t know. Packed with information. 

Now during my second pregnancy I’ve come back to it! Only thing I would wish is that it had a few more everyday things to do. Just because some of the things I already know now and don’t find it as exciting. Don’t know what exactly they should add lol but something. Maybe questionnaires, games or something. I guess I’m crazy obsessive about what this little nugget is up to inside me. And despite having a toddler now, I have too much time on my hands still 🤣. 

One other thing is that some articles about certain things to be aware of, should be mentioned earlier. Such as diabetes, preeclampsia, ectopic pregnancy etc, just because sometimes they come during or after the period where these things could have already been checked for. At which point the article becomes useless.

reviews.title: Don’t need any other apps
reviews.contents: The day I found out I was pregnant I downloaded a bunch of apps I found on the store but I ended up deleting them all EXCEPT this one. Every single day it gives you new tips and insights for each part of your pregnancy, and if anything it made me feel less crazy, when I was feeling movements for the first time or pains in random parts of my body that I didn’t even know partnered with pregnancy, the app had all the answers and put my mind at ease, it was also amazing that it has a CGI baby and if you click on her you see her move and it just makes everything more exciting and real! It also keeps you updated every week on how big your baby is, by showing you the baby’s size by either “sweet” “animal” or “fruit” which again was just amazing. For a free app it goes above and beyond! Also no annoying pop ups or adds getting in the way. Now my baby is a week old il be continuing my experience with the next stage of their app “baby +”

reviews.title: Amazing App
reviews.contents:
I have been using this app since the beginning of pregnancy and it has helped me the most out of all the apps and websites. Even over the Nhs. Every day has 2 new articles to read and I have found that a lot of stuff I didn’t know, I’ve read the article and then it’s actually happened to me so I have been less scared of the changes as I’m much more prepared for them. 
I love the weekly update on the baby development and comparison in size and also that you can share the size comparison with friends and family which has really helped me during covid. 
The time line is great as can see at a glance what’s to come. The fact you can also keep record of your bump pics and weight all in the free version. I have now upgraded to the paid version as found for the value I was getting even more like the count the kicks part which is good to have all in the one app. I will continue to use the app and move onto the baby+ after.

reviews.title: The only pregnancy app you need
reviews.contents: When I found out I was pregnant I downloaded a few different apps for information - and quickly deleted them when I realised this covers everything you need, without being cluttered or confusing. I happily upgraded to the paid version and now at 38 weeks pregnant I can say I’ve enjoyed reading the updates every single day. It’s also helped me to pack my hospital bag, to shop for my new baby, to track my weight, and to keep photos of my growing bump. It really does do it all. And I’ve looked forward to the weekly update about my baby’s development which is fascinating every time. The shiny new look just makes it even better, rather than when some apps have an overhaul and look worse! I’ve already downloaded Baby+ for when my baby arrives. I never usually write reviews but I just wanted to say thank you for being such a big part of my first pregnancy. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Excited grandparent
reviews.contents:
My daughter is expecting our first grandchild and she downloaded this app and encouraged me to download it too. She found out early on so  we have been following the 3D image from just 4 weeks.  It’s great how you can set it to “grand parent” and also add the babies name once the gender is confirmed. I love checking the growth each week and it telling me “your daughter is …. Weeks pregnant” and seeing the size scale of baby and how much it grows and weighs weekly and what baby can do this week.  

Regarding the app - as well as the 3D lifelike baby and scan images it gives lots of current information regarding pregnancy and birth which can be different from the experience we had a couple of decades ago so it keeps you in the loop.  It’s a free app with no pressure to buy things further or annoying adverts making it a pleasurable experience to use.   10/10 !!  Fully recommend

reviews.title: Just wow
reviews.contents: I’m 22 years old, and we’re expecting our first child later on this year. We’re only 9 weeks pregnant but i’ve had this app since I found out (about 5 weeks ago) and it’s by FAR the BEST app I have! In depth information, photos both 2D and 3D - looks awesome and very realistic! Even tells you the size in chocolate/sweet, fruit and animal form. Our bubba is currently a butterfly 🙈 this app makes me very excited for the future ahead and I can’t praise this app enough! It’s rare I review things but this app just needed the credit it deserves. If you want to pay the extra (which isn’t much) it even has the baby kicking timer, and contractions timer for when you’re in labour. Even has a ‘to buy’ and ‘to do’ list. Best feature is baby names section! Go through the list, heart the ones you love, and it appears on a new list of baby names just for you. For a free app it works wonders. Thank you for this app☺️

reviews.title: Love love love this app !!!!
reviews.contents: Such an all round helpful and very informative app to have I have loved using this it’s also great to have without having to unlock and pay the extra although I would have definitely, it would be Worth it  I only started using this when I found out how many weeks I was and when my due date is that’s is why I didn’t pay for extra but I have used this from the very start otherwise it does require certain details, I’m now at the very end and it’s bang on the details are so clear and easy to understand and also interesting to read and learn about you also get to see week by week how your baby develops and also how your body changes, what your symptoms could be perfect app to have definitely be using it again as this is my first child I’ll be sure to pay for the upgrade for second 👶🏻
